contract_vocabulary.SUPPORTED: The product implements the user-visible workflow, not merely a refusal of it.
contract_vocabulary.SAFE_REFUSAL_REQUIRED: The correct contract is to stop with no unsafe write. A tested refusal can satisfy this contract. It does not satisfy a different row whose contract is SUPPORTED or NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
contract_vocabulary.NOT_IMPLEMENTED: The desired workflow is absent. A tested refusal of an execute attempt belongs on the refusal row and does not move this row to SUPPORTED.

pass_policy: No operation is PASS. CI job success without a retrieved per-test transcript, and component tests that do not cover every stated invariant, stay PARTIAL. why_66_is_not_69.issue_66: Containment. Before reset or replay, classify the fetched tip against checkpoint P and observed tip O. Rewrites of already-synced history are quarantined. Polling works without webhooks. Qualified fast-forward and merge-DAG descendants may replay. Patch-id equality is not proof that work is already in SVN. Closing #66 did not implement refresh and did not authorize arbitrary rewrite replay.
why_66_is_not_69.issue_69: Coordinated history-preserving refresh. The default is update-pair-from-parent: keep published Git commits and committed SVN revisions, report unsynced work on both sides, and later append one reconciliation commit and one SVN merge revision. Re-anchor is a separate explicit mode. On this tree, preview is implemented and execute/re-anchor return not-implemented. PR 194 is unpublished work toward execution.
why_66_is_not_69.cherry_pick_and_squash: A new descendant SHA is new work under #66 even when the diff matches an already-synced commit. That can duplicate SVN content. It is not the #69 refresh algorithm, which must not replay inherited commits.
